q: Who counts the electricity for reefer containers plugged in at a port?
title: Reefer plugs at the port: whose scope
short: The terminal pays the power bill, so the electricity for reefer plugs is in the terminal's Scope 2 unless it is billed on to the shipping line as metered use. The cargo owner sees it inside the reefer freight figure. Count it once.

ul: Terminal pays and absorbs it: terminal Scope 2.
Terminal bills metered power to the line: line's Scope 2 or Scope 3.
Exporter: inside the reefer freight emissions.

p: Reefer plug hours or metered kWh per container. That turns a site total into a per-box figure a food exporter can use.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
